# Varkala Ridge Municipal Council — Water Supply Tariff and Regulations 2026–27

Approved by Council Resolution No. 117/2026 on 28 February 2026. Effective from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027. Issued by the Water Works Department, Municipal Office, Lake Road.

## 1. Introduction

The Varkala Ridge Municipal Council supplies treated water to about 38,000 households and 2,100 commercial connections. Raw water is drawn from Lake Kayalkara and treated at the Ridge Treatment Plant, which has a capacity of 42 million litres per day. Treated water is tested daily at the plant and weekly at 60 sampling points across the town. The council's target is to keep total dissolved solids (TDS) of supplied water below 450 ppm. In the dry months of March to May, TDS in the eastern wards can rise to about 700 ppm because water is drawn from deeper wells to supplement the lake.

## 2. Supply Hours

Water is supplied twice daily in all wards: from 5:30 AM to 8:30 AM and from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM. Wards 14 to 19, which are at higher elevation, receive water in the morning slot only, from 5:00 AM to 9:00 AM, during the dry months. Planned interruptions are announced at least 48 hours in advance through the council's SMS service and local newspapers.

## 3. Domestic Tariff

Domestic connections are billed every two months. The charge depends on the volume used in the billing period, measured in kilolitres (1 kilolitre = 1,000 litres).

| Consumption slab (kilolitres per two months) | Rate (INR per kilolitre) |
|---|---|
| 0 to 10 | 4.50 |
| 10 to 30 | 9.00 |
| 30 to 50 | 16.00 |
| above 50 | 28.00 |

In addition, every domestic connection pays a fixed meter charge of INR 60 per bill. Households with a below-poverty-line (BPL) card receive the first 10 kilolitres free of charge in each billing period.

## 4. Commercial and Institutional Tariff

Commercial connections, including hotels, restaurants and shops, are billed monthly at a flat rate of INR 32 per kilolitre, plus a meter charge of INR 250 per bill. Educational institutions, hospitals and places of worship pay a concessional rate of INR 14 per kilolitre. The Northbridge Institute of Technology is billed under the institutional category and has a separate bulk supply agreement for its hostels.

## 5. New Connections

| Item | Charge (INR) |
|---|---|
| Domestic connection fee | 3,500 |
| Commercial connection fee | 12,000 |
| Road cutting and restoration (per metre) | 850 |
| Meter (if supplied by the council) | 2,200 |
| Security deposit, domestic | 1,000 |
| Security deposit, commercial | 5,000 |

Applications are processed within 21 working days. A connection is sanctioned only if the property has a registered building plan and a sump or storage tank of at least 1,000 litres.

## 6. Payment, Late Fees and Disconnection

Bills must be paid within 21 days of the bill date. A late payment surcharge of 2 percent per month is added on unpaid amounts. If a bill remains unpaid for 90 days, the council may disconnect the supply after giving 15 days' written notice. Reconnection costs INR 500 for domestic and INR 2,000 for commercial connections, after all dues are paid.

Bills can be paid online on the council website, at the Municipal Office, or at any of the 12 "Jal Seva" kiosks. A rebate of 1 percent is given on domestic bills paid online within 7 days of the bill date.

## 7. Water Quality Complaints

Residents who notice discoloured or foul-smelling water should call the Water Works helpline at 0472-266-1180. The department must collect a sample within 24 hours and share test results within 72 hours. If the water is found unfit for drinking, the council supplies drinking water by tanker free of charge until the problem is fixed.

The council recommends household purification for residents in the eastern wards during the dry months. Domestic purifiers rated for TDS up to 2,000 ppm are adequate for municipal supply in all wards.

## 8. Conservation Rules

Using a hose to wash vehicles or pavements with municipal water is not permitted between 1 March and 31 May. The fine is INR 1,000 for a first offence and INR 5,000 for a repeat offence. Rainwater harvesting is mandatory for all new buildings with a roof area above 100 square metres; buildings that comply receive a 5 percent rebate on the property tax.

# Lumora Home Appliances — Service Plans and Warranty Terms (India)

Applies to all Lumora water purifiers, air purifiers and kitchen appliances sold in India on or after 1 January 2026. Customer care: 1800-419-2020 (toll free, 8:00 AM to 9:00 PM, all days).

## 1. Standard Warranty by Product

The standard warranty starts on the date of installation, or 15 days after the date of purchase if the product is not installed by then, whichever is earlier.

| Product | Standard warranty | Key part warranty |
|---|---|---|
| Aquila X2 water purifier | 2 years | UV LED module, 3 years |
| Aquila X2 Pro water purifier | 3 years | RO membrane, 3 years; heating element, 2 years |
| Aquila Mini water purifier | 1 year | none |
| Zephyr A400 air purifier | 1 year | motor, 5 years |
| Zephyr A700 air purifier | 2 years | motor, 7 years |
| Brava induction cooktop | 1 year | coil, 3 years |

Consumables are never covered by the standard warranty. Consumables include all water filters and membranes (except where a key part warranty above says otherwise), air purifier HEPA and carbon filters, sanitising sachets and cleaning kits.

## 2. Registration

Products must be registered on the Lumora app within 30 days of installation for the warranty to be valid. If a customer cannot use the app, the dealer can register the product on the customer's behalf by calling the dealer helpline. Products that are not registered receive only the minimum statutory warranty of 6 months.

## 3. What the Warranty Does Not Cover

- Damage caused by incorrect installation by anyone other than a Lumora-authorised technician.
- Damage from power surges where the product was not connected through a surge-protected socket. The Aquila X2 Pro has built-in surge protection, so this exclusion does not apply to it.
- Damage caused by water with total dissolved solids (TDS) above the model's rated limit: 2,000 ppm for the X2, 3,000 ppm for the X2 Pro and 1,000 ppm for the Aquila Mini.
- Cosmetic damage, such as scratches and dents, that does not affect operation.
- Products used for commercial purposes, such as in restaurants or offices with more than 20 people.

## 4. Service Visits and Charges

Service requests are raised through the app or by phone. Lumora aims to send a technician within 48 hours in metro cities and within 72 hours elsewhere. During the warranty period, service visits and labour are free. After the warranty ends, a visit charge of INR 399 applies, plus the cost of parts. The visit charge is waived if the customer buys a CarePlus plan during the same visit.

Repairs that cannot be done at home are taken to the nearest Lumora Service Centre. If a repair takes more than 7 days, the customer is offered a loaner purifier free of charge until the repair is complete.

## 5. CarePlus Plans

CarePlus plans extend the warranty and include some consumables. They can be bought at any time while the standard warranty is active, or within 60 days after it ends (an inspection fee of INR 299 applies in that case).

| Plan | Extra cover | Price for Aquila X2 (INR) | Price for Aquila X2 Pro (INR) | Filters included |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CarePlus 1 | 1 year | 1,999 | 2,799 | one sediment pre-filter |
| CarePlus 3 | 3 years | 4,999 | 6,499 | all filters except the RO membrane |
| CarePlus Total 5 | 5 years | 8,499 | 10,999 | all filters including the RO membrane |

CarePlus Total 5 also includes two free sanitisation visits per year. CarePlus plans are transferable once if the product is sold, for a transfer fee of INR 500.

## 6. Replacement Policy

If the same fault occurs three times within 12 months during the warranty period and cannot be repaired, Lumora replaces the product with a new unit of the same or a higher model. The replacement unit carries the remaining warranty of the original product, or 6 months, whichever is longer.

## 7. Refunds and Cancellations

A product may be returned for a full refund within 10 days of installation if it has a manufacturing defect confirmed by a technician. CarePlus plans can be cancelled within 15 days of purchase for a full refund; after that, a pro-rata refund is given minus a cancellation charge of INR 250, and no refund is given if any free filter has already been supplied.

## 8. Data and Privacy

The Lumora app collects water usage, filter life and error codes to provide service reminders. This data is stored on servers in Mumbai and is deleted 24 months after the product is de-registered. Customers can request a copy of their data or its deletion through the app's Privacy menu; requests are completed within 30 days.

# Helios Analytics Pvt. Ltd. — Leave and Holiday Policy

Effective date: 1 January 2026. Policy owner: People Operations. Version 2.4.

## 1. Leave Year

The leave year runs from 1 January to 31 December. Leave is credited monthly. Employees who join part-way through the year receive leave on a pro-rata basis from the month they join.

## 2. Types of Leave

| Leave type | Days per year | Carry forward | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Earned leave | 21 | Up to 30 days in total | Credited at 1.75 days per month |
| Sick leave | 10 | Not carried forward | Medical certificate needed for 3+ consecutive days |
| Casual leave | 6 | Not carried forward | Maximum 2 consecutive days |
| Wellness days | 4 | Not carried forward | Company-wide fixed dates, announced in January |
| Volunteering leave | 2 | Not carried forward | For registered non-profit activities |

Earned leave beyond the 30-day carry-forward cap lapses on 31 December. Employees may encash up to 10 days of earned leave per year at their basic salary rate; requests for encashment are made in November.

## 3. Applying for Leave

Leave is requested in the HR system "Peoplepad". Earned leave of five or more days must be requested at least 14 days in advance. Casual leave should be requested at least one working day in advance, except in emergencies. Sick leave can be applied for after the employee returns, within three working days.

Managers must approve or decline leave requests within three working days. If a manager does not respond, the request is approved automatically.

## 4. Parental Leave

- Birth parents receive 26 weeks of paid parental leave for the first two children and 12 weeks for the third and subsequent children.
- Non-birth parents, including adoptive parents and partners, receive 6 weeks of paid parental leave, which may be taken within 12 months of the child's birth or adoption.
- Adoptive primary caregivers of a child under 3 months old receive 12 weeks of paid leave.

After returning from parental leave, employees may work a reduced schedule of 30 hours a week for up to 8 weeks at full pay.

## 5. Bereavement and Special Leave

Employees receive 5 days of paid bereavement leave on the death of an immediate family member and 2 days for other relatives. Marriage leave is 3 days and may be taken once during employment. Employees called for jury service or to vote receive paid time off for the time required.

## 6. Public Holidays

Helios observes 10 public holidays a year: 3 national holidays (Republic Day, Independence Day and Gandhi Jayanti) and 7 festival holidays chosen by each office from a list published by People Operations in December. Employees who are required to work on a public holiday receive a compensatory day off, which must be used within 60 days.

## 7. Sabbatical

Employees with at least 5 years of continuous service may apply for an unpaid sabbatical of 1 to 6 months. One sabbatical may be taken every 5 years. Employees with 7 or more years of service receive the first 4 weeks of a sabbatical at full pay. Health insurance continues during a sabbatical.

## 8. Notice Period and Leave

During the notice period, earned leave may only be taken with the manager's approval. Unused earned leave is paid out in the final settlement, up to a maximum of 30 days. Leave taken in excess of the leave balance is deducted from the final settlement at the employee's daily gross salary.

## 9. Contacts

Questions should go to People Operations at the internal helpdesk, category "Leave". The Leave Administrator is Ms. Priyanka Achterberg.

# Aquila X2 Smart Water Purifier — User Manual

## 1. Overview

The Aquila X2 is a countertop water purifier made by Lumora Home Appliances. It combines a sediment pre-filter, an activated carbon block, a reverse osmosis (RO) membrane and an ultraviolet (UV) LED chamber. A mineral cartridge adds calcium and magnesium back into the purified water after the RO stage. The X2 stores up to 8.5 litres of purified water in a food-grade tank and can purify about 18 litres per hour when the incoming water pressure is between 0.8 and 3.5 bar.

The purifier is designed for incoming water with total dissolved solids (TDS) of up to 2,000 ppm. For water above 2,000 ppm, Lumora recommends the Aquila X2 Pro, which uses a high-rejection membrane.

## 2. Installation

Install the purifier on a flat, level surface within 1.2 metres of a power socket and a cold-water tap. Do not install the unit in direct sunlight or where the room temperature can drop below 4 °C, because freezing can crack the RO membrane housing.

Connect the inlet hose to the cold-water supply using the supplied three-way diverter valve. Connect the drain hose to a sink drain or an outlet at least 15 centimetres below the base of the unit. Before first use, flush the system by running it for 12 minutes and discarding all the water produced. The first two full tanks after installation should also be discarded.

## 3. Control Panel and Indicators

The front panel has three touch buttons: POWER, DISPENSE and HOT-LOCK. The X2 does not heat water; the HOT-LOCK button is reserved for the X2 Pro and has no function on the X2.

The status ring around the DISPENSE button shows the condition of the purifier:

- Steady blue: normal operation, tank full.
- Pulsing blue: purifying, tank filling.
- Steady amber: a filter is due for replacement within 15 days.
- Flashing amber: a filter has expired; water is still dispensed but quality is not guaranteed.
- Flashing red: error. See Section 6.

## 4. Filter Replacement Schedule

| Filter | Part number | Replace after | Typical price (INR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sediment pre-filter | AQ-SF10 | 6 months or 3,000 litres | 650 |
| Carbon block | AQ-CB22 | 12 months or 6,000 litres | 1,450 |
| RO membrane | AQ-RO75 | 24 months or 9,000 litres | 3,900 |
| UV LED module | AQ-UV3 | 36 months | 2,200 |
| Mineral cartridge | AQ-MC05 | 9 months | 980 |

Whichever limit is reached first — time or volume — applies. After replacing a filter, hold POWER and DISPENSE together for 6 seconds to reset that filter's counter. The status ring blinks green twice to confirm.

## 5. Cleaning and Maintenance

Wipe the exterior with a soft, damp cloth. Do not use abrasive cleaners or solvents. Sanitise the storage tank every 90 days using the Aquila sanitising sachet (part AQ-SAN1): drain the tank, add one sachet dissolved in two litres of water, wait 20 minutes, then drain and flush with three full tanks of purified water.

If the purifier will not be used for more than 10 days, switch it off at the mains, close the inlet valve and drain the tank. When restarting, discard the first full tank.

## 6. Troubleshooting and Error Codes

When the status ring flashes red, the small display under the panel shows an error code.

- E1 — Low inlet pressure. Check that the inlet valve is open and that the supply pressure is above 0.8 bar. A booster pump kit (AQ-BP2) is available for low-pressure homes.
- E2 — Tank overflow sensor triggered. Switch off, drain the tank and check that the float switch moves freely.
- E3 — UV module fault. The purifier stops dispensing to prevent unsterilised water being served. Contact service.
- E4 — Leak detected in the base tray. Switch off at the mains immediately and close the inlet valve.
- E5 — Membrane pressure too high, usually caused by a clogged sediment pre-filter. Replace AQ-SF10 and reset its counter.

## 7. Warranty

The Aquila X2 carries a 2-year comprehensive warranty from the date of installation, covering parts and labour, provided the unit is registered on the Lumora app within 30 days of installation. Filters and the mineral cartridge are consumables and are not covered. The UV LED module is covered for 3 years. The warranty is void if non-genuine filters are used or if the unit is serviced by anyone other than a Lumora-authorised technician.

Extended warranty plans are available: "CarePlus 1" adds one year for INR 1,999 and includes one free sediment pre-filter; "CarePlus 3" adds three years for INR 4,999 and includes all filter replacements except the RO membrane.

## 8. Specifications

Rated voltage: 220–240 V AC, 50 Hz. Power consumption: 36 W while purifying, 2 W on standby. Dimensions: 270 mm (W) × 410 mm (D) × 445 mm (H). Net weight: 7.8 kg. Recovery ratio: up to 60 percent (the share of incoming water that becomes purified water).

The Central Library, named after the Institute's founder, Dr. Hari Prasad Venkatesan, holds about 1,85,000 printed volumes and provides access to 34 online journal databases. Undergraduate students may borrow up to six books at a time for 14 days; postgraduate students may borrow up to ten books for 30 days. During the end-semester examination period it remains open 24 hours.

# Helios Analytics Pvt. Ltd. — Travel and Expense Policy

Effective date: 1 April 2026. Policy owner: Finance. Version 5.0. This policy replaces version 4.3.

## 1. Scope

This policy covers business travel and work-related expenses for all employees of Helios Analytics in India. It does not cover relocation, which is handled under the Relocation Policy, or the home office allowance, which is covered by the Remote and Hybrid Work Policy.

## 2. Approvals

All business travel must be approved in advance in the travel tool "Wayfarer". Domestic trips need approval from the employee's manager. International trips need approval from the manager and the department head, and must be requested at least 21 days before departure. Trips that are booked without approval will not be reimbursed unless the department head approves an exception in writing within 7 days of the trip.

## 3. Air and Rail Travel

Employees may fly economy class on all domestic flights. Premium economy is allowed on international flights longer than 6 hours. Business class is allowed only for the CEO and the CFO, or with written approval from the CEO.

Flights must be booked through Wayfarer at least 14 days in advance when possible. For trips booked less than 7 days before departure, the employee must record a reason. Rail travel in AC 2-tier or AC chair car is allowed for journeys under 8 hours.

## 4. Hotels

Hotels must be booked through Wayfarer. The nightly limits, including taxes, are:

| City category | Examples | Nightly hotel limit (INR) |
|---|---|---|
| Tier 1 | Mumbai, Delhi NCR, Bengaluru | 7,500 |
| Tier 2 | Pune, Hyderabad, Chennai, Kolkata, Ahmedabad | 6,000 |
| Tier 3 | All other cities | 4,500 |

During Helios Converge week in Pune, the company books a block of rooms at the partner hotel and employees must stay there. Staying with friends or family instead of a hotel earns a flat "home stay" allowance of INR 1,500 per night.

## 5. Daily Allowance

Employees travelling overnight receive a daily allowance (per diem) to cover meals and incidental expenses. No receipts are needed for the per diem.

- Domestic travel: INR 1,800 per day in Tier 1 cities, INR 1,400 per day elsewhere.
- International travel: USD 75 per day, or USD 95 per day in the United States, the United Kingdom, Singapore and Switzerland.

On the day of departure and the day of return, half the daily allowance is paid. If meals are provided by a client or at a conference, the allowance is reduced by 25 percent for each meal provided.

## 6. Local Transport

Taxis and ride-hailing services are allowed for business trips and for travel to client sites. Employees using their own car are reimbursed INR 12 per kilometre; for two-wheelers the rate is INR 5 per kilometre. Parking and tolls are reimbursed at actual cost with receipts. Travel between home and the employee's regular office is not reimbursable, except for late-night travel after 10:30 PM, which is reimbursed up to INR 800 per trip.

## 7. Client Entertainment

Client meals and entertainment must be pre-approved by the manager when the expected cost is above INR 10,000. The limit is INR 3,000 per attendee, including the Helios employees present. Alcohol is reimbursable only when a client is present and is limited to 20 percent of the bill.

## 8. Claims and Reimbursement

Expense claims are submitted in "Ledgerly", the same expense portal used for the home office allowance. Every expense above INR 500 must have a receipt. Claims must be submitted within 45 days of the end of the trip; claims submitted between 45 and 90 days late need department head approval, and claims older than 90 days are rejected. Approved claims are paid with the next monthly salary if approved by the 20th of the month.

Corporate cards are issued to employees who travel more than six times a year. The monthly limit on a corporate card is INR 1,50,000. Personal expenses must never be charged to a corporate card; if this happens by mistake, the employee must repay the amount within 15 days.

## 9. Misuse

Submitting false or inflated claims is gross misconduct and may lead to dismissal. Finance audits a random sample of 10 percent of claims every quarter.

## 10. Contacts

Questions should go to the Finance helpdesk, category "Travel & Expenses". The Head of Finance Operations is Mr. Rohan Vasquez-Iyer.

# Helios Analytics Pvt. Ltd. — Remote and Hybrid Work Policy

Effective date: 1 March 2026. Policy owner: People Operations. Version 3.2.

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This policy explains how employees of Helios Analytics may work away from the office. It applies to all full-time and fixed-term employees in India. It does not apply to interns, who must work from an office for at least four days a week during their first eight weeks, or to contractors, whose arrangements are set in their individual contracts.

## 2. Work Arrangements

Helios offers three arrangements:

- **Office-first:** at least four days a week in an office.
- **Hybrid:** two "anchor days" in the office each week, chosen by the team. For most teams the anchor days are Tuesday and Thursday. The Data Platform team uses Monday and Wednesday.
- **Remote:** fully remote work, approved by the department head and People Operations. Remote employees must still attend the quarterly in-person planning week, called "Helios Converge", which is held in Pune.

New joiners start on the hybrid arrangement and may apply for remote work only after completing their 6-month probation period with a performance rating of "Meets Expectations" or higher.

## 3. Core Hours and Availability

All employees, regardless of arrangement, must be available during core hours of 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM IST on working days. Outside core hours, employees may set their own schedules as long as they complete a 40-hour week. Employees must respond to messages from their manager within two hours during core hours.

Meetings must not be scheduled before 10:00 AM or after 6:30 PM IST unless at least one participant is in a time zone where no other slot is reasonable.

## 4. Home Office Allowance

Employees on the hybrid or remote arrangement receive a one-time home office setup allowance of INR 25,000, which can be claimed within the first 90 days of moving to that arrangement. Eligible items are a desk, an ergonomic chair, a monitor, a keyboard and mouse, and a headset. Laptops are provided by the company and are not covered by the allowance.

Remote employees also receive a monthly internet and utilities allowance of INR 2,200. Hybrid employees receive INR 1,100 per month. The allowance is paid with salary and is taxable.

Receipts must be uploaded to the expense portal "Ledgerly" within 30 days of purchase. Claims submitted later will be rejected.

## 5. Working From Another Location

Employees may work from a location other than their registered home address for up to 30 days per calendar year without approval, provided the location is within India and has a reliable internet connection of at least 50 Mbps. Working from outside India for any period requires written approval from the Legal team at least 21 days in advance, because of tax and data protection rules. Working from outside India is limited to 15 working days per calendar year.

## 6. Security Requirements

Employees working away from the office must:

- Connect only through the company VPN ("HeliosGate") when accessing internal systems.
- Never use public Wi-Fi without the VPN.
- Lock their screen whenever they step away; laptops lock automatically after 5 minutes of inactivity.
- Store client data only on company-approved systems. Downloading client data to personal devices is a disciplinary offence.

Lost or stolen devices must be reported to the IT Service Desk within 4 hours of discovery.

## 7. Changing or Ending an Arrangement

An employee may request a change of arrangement once every six months. The manager must respond within 10 working days. Helios may end a remote or hybrid arrangement with 30 days' written notice if business needs change or if performance falls below "Meets Expectations" for two consecutive review cycles.

## 8. Contacts

Questions about this policy should go to People Operations at the internal helpdesk, category "Workplace". The Head of People Operations is Ms. Ifeoma Desai-Brandt.

# Northbridge Institute of Technology — Student Handbook 2026–27

## 1. About the Institute

The Northbridge Institute of Technology (NIT-B) was founded in 1987 in the lakeside town of Varkala Ridge. It began as a polytechnic with three departments: Civil Engineering, Electrical Engineering and Applied Chemistry. In 2004 it was granted autonomous status by the Regional Board of Technical Education, which allows it to design its own curriculum and conduct its own examinations. The Institute today has eleven departments, roughly 6,400 students and 410 full-time faculty members. The campus covers 212 acres and includes a 40-acre wetland reserve that is maintained jointly with the Varkala Ridge Ecological Trust.

The current Director is Prof. Meenakshi Raghavan, who took office in July 2023. The Dean of Student Affairs is Dr. Tobias Okonkwo-Lindqvist. Students should address academic grievances first to their department's Faculty Advisor, then to the Dean of Academics, and only then to the Director's office.

The Institute's motto is "Measure twice, build once." The official colours are slate blue and amber.

## 2. Academic Calendar

The academic year is divided into two regular semesters and an optional summer term.

The Monsoon Semester runs from 4 August to 12 December. The Spring Semester runs from 5 January to 30 April. The Summer Term is a seven-week intensive session that begins on 18 May and is restricted to backlog courses and approved minor-credit electives.

Mid-semester examinations are held in the eighth week of each regular semester. End-semester examinations occupy the final two weeks. Results are published within 21 calendar days of the last examination.

Registration for each semester closes nine days after classes begin. A student who has not registered by that date must apply for late registration, which is allowed only up to the end of the third week and carries a late fee (see Section 4).

## 3. Attendance Policy

Attendance is recorded in every lecture, tutorial and laboratory session. A student must maintain at least 78 percent attendance in each course to be eligible to sit the end-semester examination in that course. Medical leave supported by a certificate from the Campus Health Centre may be counted towards attendance, up to a maximum of 10 percent of the total sessions in a course.

A student whose attendance falls between 70 and 78 percent may appeal to the Attendance Review Committee, which meets in the eleventh week of each semester. Appeals must be filed through the student portal at least five working days before the committee meets. Attendance below 70 percent cannot be condoned under any circumstances, and the student receives a grade of "XA" (debarred for attendance) in that course.

Laboratory courses have a stricter rule: a student who misses more than two laboratory sessions without a medical certificate must complete make-up sessions, which are scheduled on Saturdays and cost a fee per session.

## 4. Fees and Charges

All fees are payable in Indian Rupees through the student portal. The table below lists the standard charges for the 2026–27 academic year.

| Item | Amount (INR) | When payable |
|---|---|---|
| Tuition fee (B.Tech, per semester) | 1,18,500 | Before registration |
| Tuition fee (M.Tech, per semester) | 96,000 | Before registration |
| Hostel accommodation (twin sharing, per semester) | 42,750 | Before registration |
| Hostel accommodation (single room, per semester) | 61,200 | Before registration |
| Mess charges (per month) | 5,850 | Monthly, by the 10th |
| Examination fee (per semester) | 3,400 | With tuition |
| Late registration fee | 2,500 | At late registration |
| Laboratory make-up session (per session) | 750 | Before the session |
| Transcript (per copy) | 400 | On request |
| Degree certificate re-issue | 3,000 | On request |
| Caution deposit (refundable, one time) | 15,000 | At admission |

A late payment penalty of 1.5 percent per month is charged on any tuition fee not paid by the registration deadline. Students from families with an annual income below INR 6,00,000 may apply for a tuition waiver of up to 60 percent through the Financial Aid Office. Waiver applications for the Monsoon Semester must be submitted by 15 June.

The caution deposit is refunded within 45 days after the student graduates or withdraws, minus any outstanding dues or damage charges.

## 5. Grading System

NIT-B uses a ten-point grading scale. The letter grades and their grade points are: O (10), A+ (9), A (8), B+ (7), B (6), C (5), P (4) and F (0). A grade of P is the minimum passing grade. The Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA) is the credit-weighted mean of the grade points earned in that semester. The Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) is the credit-weighted mean over all semesters.

A student who receives an F may re-register for the course in a later semester or in the Summer Term. The higher of the two grades is used in CGPA calculations, but both attempts appear on the transcript.

To graduate with distinction, a B.Tech student must earn a CGPA of at least 8.75 with no F grades at any point. A student on academic probation — defined as an SGPA below 5.0 in any semester — may register for no more than 18 credits in the following semester.

## 6. Hostel Rules

Hostel residents must return to their hostel by 10:30 PM on weekdays and 11:30 PM on Fridays and Saturdays. Guests are allowed in the common lounge between 9:00 AM and 7:00 PM only. Cooking appliances, including induction plates and electric kettles above 1,000 watts, are not permitted in rooms.

Hostel allocation for first-year students is done by lottery. Senior students are allocated rooms according to their CGPA, with ties broken by attendance percentage. A student who violates hostel rules three times in one semester may be asked to vacate the hostel, with no refund of the hostel fee for that semester.

# Northbridge Institute of Technology — Scholarships and Financial Aid Guide 2026–27

Issued by the Financial Aid Office, Administrative Block B, Room 214. Office hours are 10:00 AM to 4:30 PM, Monday to Friday. The Financial Aid Officer is Mr. Anirudh Kesavan.

## 1. Overview

Every year the Institute distributes about INR 4.2 crore in scholarships, waivers and emergency grants. Roughly one student in five receives some form of financial support. Aid is awarded on the basis of merit, need, or both, and each scheme has its own deadline. A student may hold at most two scholarships at the same time, but the combined value of all awards may not exceed the student's total tuition and hostel charges for the year.

Applications are made through the "Aid" tab of the student portal. Paper applications are accepted only from students who have no reliable internet access, and must be handed in at Room 214 in person.

## 2. Merit Scholarships

**Founder's Merit Scholarship.** Named after Dr. Hari Prasad Venkatesan. Awarded to the top 25 students of each incoming B.Tech batch, ranked by the entrance examination score. The scholarship covers 75 percent of the tuition fee for all eight semesters, provided the student keeps a CGPA of at least 8.0. If the CGPA falls below 8.0 in any year, the scholarship is suspended for the following year and can be restored once the CGPA is back above 8.0. It is not restored for semesters that have already passed.

**Department Rank Award.** A one-time cash award of INR 20,000 given each year to the student with the highest SGPA in each department and year of study. In the event of a tie, the award is split equally.

**Lakeside Research Fellowship.** For M.Tech students who publish a paper in a recognised journal or conference during their programme. The fellowship pays INR 12,000 per month for up to 10 months and is renewable once. Applications are reviewed by the Research Council, which meets in the first week of February and the first week of September.

## 3. Need-Based Support

**Tuition Waiver Scheme.** Students whose annual family income is below INR 6,00,000 may receive a tuition waiver. The waiver depends on income band:

| Annual family income (INR) | Tuition waiver |
|---|---|
| Below 2,50,000 | 60 percent |
| 2,50,000 to 4,00,000 | 40 percent |
| 4,00,000 to 6,00,000 | 25 percent |

The waiver does not cover hostel, mess or examination fees. Income must be documented with an income certificate issued within the previous 12 months. Waiver applications for the Monsoon Semester must be submitted by 15 June, and for the Spring Semester by 20 November.

**Hostel Subsidy.** Students who hold a tuition waiver of 40 percent or more may also apply for a hostel subsidy of INR 15,000 per semester. The subsidy is credited directly against the hostel fee and cannot be paid out in cash.

**Book Grant.** First-year students on the Tuition Waiver Scheme receive a one-time book grant of INR 6,500 in the form of a library-bookshop voucher. The voucher expires 90 days after it is issued.

## 4. Emergency Assistance

The Student Emergency Fund helps students facing a sudden financial crisis, such as a medical emergency in the family or the loss of a parent's income. Grants are up to INR 50,000 per student per academic year and do not need to be repaid. Requests are reviewed within five working days. In urgent medical cases the Dean of Student Affairs can approve up to INR 15,000 on the same day.

Interest-free short-term loans of up to INR 30,000 are also available. They must be repaid within 12 months, in monthly instalments deducted from any stipend or paid through the portal. A student with an unpaid emergency loan cannot receive a degree certificate until the loan is cleared.

## 5. External Scholarships

The Financial Aid Office helps students apply for government and private scholarships. Students who receive an external scholarship must inform the office within 30 days, because some Institute awards are reduced when an external scholarship is received. In particular, the Founder's Merit Scholarship is reduced by the amount of any external tuition scholarship so that the combined tuition support does not exceed 100 percent.

## 6. Work-Study Programme

The Campus Work-Study Programme offers part-time jobs in the library, laboratories, the IT help desk and the Sports Complex. Students may work up to 12 hours per week during the semester and up to 30 hours per week during vacations. The hourly rate is INR 180 for undergraduates and INR 240 for postgraduates. Work-study earnings are paid monthly into the student's bank account on the 5th of the following month.

To be eligible, a student must have a CGPA of at least 6.0 and no disciplinary record. First-semester students may join only after their mid-semester examinations.

## 7. Repayment, Withdrawal and Appeals

If a student withdraws from the Institute before the end of a semester, any scholarship or waiver amount for that semester must be repaid on a pro-rata basis. Appeals against aid decisions can be made to the Financial Aid Appeals Panel within 15 days of the decision. The panel's decision is final.

Students found to have given false information in an aid application must repay the full amount received and may be referred to the Disciplinary Board.
